project.name: Jarvis
project.description: A voice-first local coding assistant powered by Claude API, featuring hands-free voice interaction with wake word detection, streaming TTS responses, and proactive monitoring via Telegram. Integrates LangGraph for agent orchestration, Voxtral for real-time STT, CSM/Kokoro for TTS, and includes Google Calendar/Gmail integration.

nodes.name: Settings
nodes.description: Central configuration class using Pydantic BaseSettings. Manages all Jarvis settings including LLM, STT/TTS, audio, wake word, workspace safety, Google, web search, memory, Telegram, and proactive monitors. Loads from .env file with JARVIS_ prefix.

nodes.name: get_settings
nodes.description: Returns singleton Settings instance. Creates new instance on first call.

nodes.name: reload_settings
nodes.description: Forces reload of Settings instance from environment. Used for testing or when env vars change.

nodes.name: ToolError
nodes.description: Exception raised by tool implementations when operations fail (e.g., path outside workspace, file too large, disabled features).

nodes.name: Toolbox
nodes.description: Unified tool registry and dispatcher for all Jarvis tools. Routes tool calls to coding, web, memory, calendar, email, and notification handlers. Provides async dispatch method with error handling.

nodes.name: read_file
nodes.description: Reads a file from workspace with optional line slicing. Enforces MAX_FILE_BYTES (200KB) limit. Returns numbered lines.

nodes.name: list_dir
nodes.description: Lists directory contents, sorted with directories first. Hides dotfiles.

nodes.name: grep
nodes.description: Regex search across files with glob filtering. Returns up to MAX_GREP_MATCHES (200) results. Skips .pyc and .git files.

nodes.name: write_file
nodes.description: Writes content to file if JARVIS_ALLOW_WRITES is enabled. Creates parent directories.

nodes.name: run_shell
nodes.description: Executes shell command in workspace if JARVIS_ALLOW_SHELL is enabled. Blocks dangerous commands (rm -rf /, mkfs, fork bombs). Enforces timeout and output truncation.

nodes.name: dispatch
nodes.description: Central async dispatcher for all tool calls. Routes to appropriate handler based on tool name. Returns error strings on failure.

nodes.name: TOOL_SCHEMAS
nodes.description: OpenAI-style function schemas for all 21 tools: coding (read_file, list_dir, grep, write_file, run_shell), web (web_search, fetch_page), memory (remember, recall, forget), calendar (list_events, create_event, update_event, find_free_slot), email (list_emails, read_email, draft_reply, send_email), and notify.

nodes.name: STT
nodes.description: Real-time speech-to-text powered by Mistral Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602. Provides <500ms transcription latency optimized for Apple Silicon (MPS) with bf16. Includes lazy loading, resampling to 16kHz, low-energy rejection, and hallucination filtering.

nodes.name: transcribe
nodes.description: Async transcription of PCM audio. Converts int16 to float32, resamples to 16kHz if needed, rejects low-energy audio (RMS < 0.001), and runs synchronous transcription in thread pool.

nodes.name: _get_device
nodes.description: Detects best available device for Voxtral inference. Priority: CUDA > MPS > CPU. Cached with lru_cache.

nodes.name: _load_voxtral
nodes.description: Loads Voxtral-Mini-4B model and processor once. Uses bf16 on MPS/CUDA, fp32 on CPU. Downloads ~8GB on first run. Cached globally.

nodes.name: _is_hallucination
nodes.description: Filters common STT hallucinations on silent/noisy input. Detects known garbage outputs (you, okay, thanks, etc.) and repeated single words.

nodes.name: test_voxtral_e2e

nodes.label: SYSTEM_PROMPT
nodes.description: Multi-line system prompt string defining Jarvis personality. Includes voice-optimized style rules (short sentences, no markdown, TTS-friendly), proactive behavior, confirmation workflow for destructive actions, and tool usage guidelines.

nodes.label: proactive_alert()
nodes.description: Formats proactive alert messages for TTS or Telegram. Takes source, situation description, and optional suggested action. Returns 'Sir, {situation}. Shall I {action}?' or 'Sir, {situation}.' if no action provided.

nodes.label: nodes.py
nodes.description: LangGraph node functions for the Jarvis agent graph. Core orchestration logic including memory retrieval, LLM interaction via claude -p subprocess, tool calling with confirmation workflow, and response handling. Implements the think-act-observe-respond cycle.

key_features: Claude CLI subprocess streaming with sentence callbacks
Tool call confirmation for destructive operations
Tool call parsing from markdown code blocks

nodes.label: retrieve_memory_node()
nodes.description: LangGraph node that retrieves relevant memories from Mem0Store based on the last user message. Returns up to 5 memories or empty list if mem0_store is None. Extracts last user message with string content from state.

nodes.label: _build_system_with_memories()
nodes.description: Private helper that augments SYSTEM_PROMPT with retrieved memories. If memories exist, appends section 'What you know about this user (strong priors, not absolute truth)' with bulleted memory list.

nodes.label: _build_claude_prompt()
nodes.description: Converts message history to single prompt string for claude -p. Wraps system in <system> tags and messages in role tags. Handles list-based content with tool_result and tool_use blocks.

metadata.note: Legacy function, not actively used by _run_claude

nodes.label: _run_claude()
nodes.description: Async function that streams claude -p subprocess. Fires sentence_callback per sentence for TTS. Runs with --permission-mode bypassPermissions, --output-format stream-json, --verbose. OAuth from macOS keychain, no API key needed. Parses stream events for text deltas.

nodes.label: think_node()
nodes.description: Main LLM reasoning node. Builds memory-augmented system prompt with tool descriptions. Runs multi-turn loop (MAX_TURNS=6) calling _run_claude, parsing tool calls from ```tool_call blocks, checking for confirmation requirements. Returns final response or pending action requiring confirmation.

nodes.label: act_node()
nodes.description: Executes tool calls via toolbox.dispatch. Iterates over state tool_calls, dispatches each, collects results. Appends tool_result messages to conversation. Returns updated messages with results.

nodes.label: observe_node()
nodes.description: Clears tool_results from state after they've been processed. Simple node that returns empty tool_results list if any existed.

nodes.label: respond_node()
nodes.description: Extracts final_response from state. If confirmation required, formats pending action message. Otherwise extracts text content from last assistant message, handling both string and list-based content formats.

nodes.label: store_memory_node()
nodes.description: Stores user and assistant messages to Mem0Store for future retrieval. Extracts last user message and final_response, stores each with appropriate role. Returns empty dict (side-effect only node).

nodes.label: CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED_TOOLS
nodes.description: Set of tool names requiring user confirmation before execution: write_file, run_shell, create_event, update_event, send_email. Used by think_node to gate destructive operations.

nodes.label: TOOL_CALL_RE
nodes.description: Regex pattern to extract tool calls from LLM output. Matches ```tool_call markdown code blocks with JSON content. Used by think_node to parse tool invocations.

nodes.label: MAX_TURNS
nodes.description: Maximum number of think-act loop iterations. Set to 6 to prevent infinite tool calling loops.

nodes.label: Voxtral Completion Report
nodes.description: Final implementation report documenting the hybrid voice architecture decision: Voxtral for STT + CSM/Kokoro for TTS. Explains why unified approach was not used (Voxtral is STT-only), test results, performance gains, and complete installation guide.

metadata.key_decision: Voxtral is STT-only, not unified S2S model - hybrid approach is optimal

layers.name: CLI Interface & Entry Points
layers.description: User-facing command-line interface and entry points. Typer-based CLI with commands for voice, chat, ask, telegram, watch, notify, auth, and service management (start, stop, status, restart).

layers.name: Agent Orchestration & State Machine
layers.description: LangGraph-based agent orchestration with state machine nodes. Manages conversation flow through retrieve-memory → think → act → observe → respond → store-memory cycle. Includes confirmation workflow for destructive operations and streaming sentence callbacks for TTS.

layers.name: Proactive Monitoring & Background Tasks
layers.description: Background monitors for calendar events, emails, and file system changes. Polls external services and invokes the agent graph to generate alerts sent via Telegram. Includes CalendarMonitor, EmailMonitor, and WatchdogMonitor.

layers.name: Core Services & Configuration
layers.description: Central configuration, session factory, and personality definition. Includes Pydantic-based settings, dependency injection for building runtime components (toolbox, graph, memory), and system prompt with personality traits.

layers.name: Tool Execution & Registry
layers.description: Unified tool registry and dispatcher for all agent capabilities. Routes tool calls to coding (read_file, list_dir, grep, write_file, run_shell), web (web_search, fetch_page), memory (remember, recall, forget), calendar, email, and notify tools. Includes workspace safety controls and schema definitions.

layers.name: Memory & Long-Term Storage
layers.description: mem0-free memory store using fastembed embeddings, Chroma vector DB, and claude CLI for fact extraction. Provides retrieve (semantic search), store (extract and save), remember (explicit storage), and forget (deletion) operations.

layers.name: Voice Pipeline (STT, TTS, Audio I/O)
layers.description: Complete voice processing pipeline. STT using Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime (<500ms latency), multi-engine TTS (CSM 1B preferred, Kokoro fallback) with phrase caching, VAD-gated audio recording, playback management, sentence streaming, and wake word detection (openWakeWord or STT fallback).

layers.name: External Integrations
layers.description: Integration layer for external services. Google OAuth 2.0 for Calendar and Gmail with credential management, Telegram bot bridge for remote chat and push notifications with access control, and web search (Brave API + DuckDuckGo fallback).

layers.name: Configuration & Environment
layers.description: Environment configuration files, build automation, and project metadata. Includes .env files with API keys and feature flags, Makefile with dev workflow automation, pyproject.toml with dependencies, and configuration components for LLM, voice engines, audio I/O, safety controls, and external services.

layers.name: Infrastructure Scripts & Utilities
layers.description: Shell scripts for model provisioning and LLM server management. Includes download_voice.sh for fetching Piper TTS models, serve_vllm.sh for starting GPU-optimized vLLM server, and wait_for_vllm.sh for health checking.

layers.name: External Models & Services
layers.description: External model dependencies and service references. Includes Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime (STT), CSM 1B (TTS), Kokoro ONNX (TTS fallback), HuggingFace model hub, and vLLM inference engine.

layers.name: Documentation

tour.title: Welcome to Jarvis: Voice-First Coding Assistant
tour.description: Start with the README to understand what Jarvis does: a voice-activated local AI assistant that listens for 'hey Jarvis', transcribes your question with Voxtral STT (<500ms latency), routes it to Claude via the CLI, and streams the answer back through CSM/Kokoro TTS sentence-by-sentence. It includes a Telegram bridge for remote chat and proactive notifications. Everything runs locally with no API keys except for Claude OAuth.

tour.title: Entry Point: CLI Commands
tour.description: The main.py entry point defines all user-facing commands via Typer: 'voice' (hands-free voice loop), 'chat' (text REPL), 'ask' (one-shot query), 'telegram' (bridge only), 'watch' (file monitoring with Telegram alerts), 'notify' (push notifications), and 'auth' (Google OAuth for Calendar/Gmail). The voice command orchestrates the entire voice pipeline including wake word detection, VAD-gated recording, STT, LLM streaming, TTS synthesis, and playback with filler phrases during long operations.

tour.title: Configuration: Pydantic Settings
tour.description: All settings live in a Pydantic BaseSettings class loaded from .env with JARVIS_ prefix. This includes LLM model/temperature, STT language, TTS engine/voice, audio devices, wake word settings, workspace safety controls (allow_writes, allow_shell), Google credentials paths, Brave API key for web search, mem0 memory toggle, Telegram token/chat IDs, and proactive monitor poll intervals. The singleton pattern ensures one Settings instance across the app.

tour.title: Agent Orchestration: LangGraph State Machine
tour.description: The agent graph is built with LangGraph nodes that form a think-act-observe-respond cycle. The flow: retrieve_memory_node loads relevant facts from Mem0Store, think_node invokes Claude via subprocess streaming, act_node executes tool calls with confirmation workflow for destructive operations (write_file, run_shell, send_email), observe_node collects results, respond_node finalizes the reply, and store_memory_node persists new facts. The graph supports up to MAX_TURNS=6 tool loops per conversation turn and streams sentences to a TTS callback for real-time audio synthesis.

tour.title: Voice Pipeline: Voxtral STT, CSM TTS, Audio I/O
tour.description: The voice pipeline combines three components: STT uses Mistral Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime for <500ms transcription latency (bf16 on MPS/CUDA), with resampling to 16kHz, low-energy rejection (RMS < 0.001), and hallucination filtering. TTS offers two engines: CSM 1B (preferred) and Kokoro ONNX (fallback), both with disk-based phrase caching for instant playback of acks/fillers. AudioIO handles VAD-gated recording with webrtcvad, echo management (tail hold + mute window), and serial playback with an Iron Man-inspired boot sound. The streaming module buffers tokens into complete sentences for TTS-friendly synthesis.

tour.title: Wake Word Detection: openWakeWord + STT Fallback
tour.description: Wake word detection uses openWakeWord with the hey_jarvis model for real-time phrase detection. If openWakeWord is unavailable, it falls back to STT-based keyword matching (fuzzy match on 'jarvis' in the transcript). The voice loop supports a wake/sleep state machine: sleeping mode ignores all input except wake phrases, and the user can toggle states via Cmd+J keyboard shortcut (macOS) or by saying 'jarvis sleep'. Each state transition plays a themed sound effect (boot chime / power-down tone) and speaks a confirmation phrase.

tour.title: Tool Execution: Coding, Web, Memory, Calendar, Email
tour.description: The unified Toolbox registry dispatches tool calls to domain-specific handlers. Coding tools (read_file, list_dir, grep, write_file, run_shell) enforce workspace boundaries, size limits (200KB max), and safety flags. Web tools (web_search via Brave API + DuckDuckGo fallback, fetch_page) enable internet access. Memory tools (remember, recall, forget) interact with the Mem0Store. Calendar tools (list_events, create_event, update_event, find_free_slot) and Email tools (list_emails, read_email, draft_reply, send_email with allow_send safety flag) integrate with Google services via OAuth 2.0. All tools are exposed as OpenAI-style function schemas in TOOL_SCHEMAS.

tour.title: Memory: Mem0Store with FastEmbed + ChromaDB
tour.description: Jarvis uses a mem0-free memory store that combines fastembed embeddings (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5), ChromaDB vector database, and Claude CLI for fact extraction. The store provides four operations: retrieve (semantic search via cosine similarity), store (extract memorable facts from text using Claude subprocess and upsert to vector DB), remember (explicit storage without extraction), and forget (delete similar embeddings). This enables Jarvis to build long-term context across conversations without requiring the paid mem0 service.

tour.title: Telegram Bridge: Remote Chat & Push Notifications
tour.description: The TelegramBridge enables remote interaction and proactive alerts. It runs a python-telegram-bot application with handlers for /start, /help, /whoami, /ask, and plain text messages. Access control via JARVIS_TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_CHATS ensures only authorized users can interact. The bridge also provides a notify method for push notifications sent to JARVIS_TELEGRAM_NOTIFY_CHAT, used by proactive monitors (calendar, email, watchdog) to alert the user about upcoming events, unread emails, or file system changes. All conversation history is maintained per-session for context continuity.

tour.title: Proactive Monitoring: Calendar, Email, Watchdog
tour.description: Jarvis runs background monitors that poll external services and trigger alerts. CalendarMonitor checks for upcoming events (default: 15 minutes before start time) and invokes the agent graph to generate natural language alerts sent via Telegram. EmailMonitor polls for new unread emails and notifies the user with sender/subject summaries. WatchdogMonitor uses watchfiles to watch filesystem paths for changes, optionally running a command (e.g., pytest) after each change and pushing the output to Telegram. All monitors support configurable poll intervals and debounce windows, and they integrate with the agent graph for intelligent alert generation.

tour.title: Personality & System Prompt: Voice-First Style
tour.description: Jarvis's personality is defined in the SYSTEM_PROMPT constant with voice-optimized style rules: short sentences (under 6 unless asked), no markdown or code fences (TTS-unfriendly), address user as 'Sir', confirm destructive actions before executing, and proactively monitor external services. The proactive_alert function formats situation/action alerts with the signature 'Sir, {situation}. Shall I {action}?' for natural spoken interaction. This prompt is augmented with retrieved memories before each LLM turn to maintain personalized context.

tour.title: Google OAuth Integration: Calendar & Gmail
tour.description: Google integration uses OAuth 2.0 with local server flow for Calendar (read/write events, find free slots) and Gmail (read/compose/send emails). The get_credentials function handles token refresh and re-authorization via browser when expired. Tokens persist to disk (~/.jarvis/google-token.json by default). The build_services factory creates ready-to-use calendar_service and gmail_service objects. These are injected into the toolbox via inject_google during session initialization, gracefully handling missing credentials with log warnings.
